transfer.scenario: A colleague in validation says: 'We set temperature to zero and return JSON, so the assistant's output is deterministic and correct.' Explain, in two or three sentences, what each setting actually gives you.
rubric: temperature zero not fully deterministic|outputs can still vary
low temperature is not correctness|consistent wrong answer possible
schema guarantees shape not truth|valid JSON can hold wrong values
still need content validation|business-rule checks|grounding check

narration.text: A language model reads text as tokens. A token can be a word, part of a word, or a single character.
Token counts depend on the model's tokenizer, so I use the provider's token counter instead of guessing from words.
The context window is the model's working memory for one call. It is not the data the model was trained on.
Everything counts toward it: the instructions, the conversation, any documents, and the answer being written.
More context is not automatically better. Quality can drop as the input grows, so I send what is relevant.
During inference the weights are fixed. The model picks one token at a time from a probability distribution.
Temperature reshapes that distribution. Lower is more consistent, but even zero is not guaranteed to repeat exactly.
Structured outputs force the reply to match a JSON schema. That guarantees the shape, not that the values are true.
